prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators

statement.case_for: Topological insulators are the strongest candidate on the shortlist on every criterion I weigh. The Kane-Mele Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall prediction (2005) introduced a genuinely new organising principle for electronic matter, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum-well experiment (2007) delivered an unambiguous transport signature of protected edge channels. Two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM across many materials make the interpretation stable. Seven of eight members place it in the top three. A single-achievement prize pairing the decisive theory with the first experimental realisation is the cleanest structure available. After reading colleagues I have moved from my opening trio (Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan) to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, because leaving out a co-author of the foundational papers is harder to defend than leaving out a later, adjacent experiment.
statement.case_against: Any three-name cut omits real contributors: Hasan's 3D ARPES discovery, and the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang is deceased, and none are on the credited list), plus the 3D theory of Fu, Kane and Mele and of Moore and Balents. The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter may also make some colleagues wary of a second topology award, and the credit boundary between the 2D and 3D stories is genuinely contestable. A prize can be criticised for either dropping Hasan or dropping Mele.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B006 first but proposes Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, treating Mele and the HgTe proposers as a fairness problem under the three-person limit.
responses.response: I opened with the same trio and I share the concern, but the colleagues' arguments have moved me. Mele is co-author of the Kane-Mele papers that carry the theoretical core; dropping him while crediting Kane alone splits one discovery. Hasan's 3D work is major, yet it builds on the 2D concept and 3D theory that is itself not fully covered by the credited names. I would rather keep the 2D theory and first-experiment pair intact, and I accept that Hasan is the omission. I would welcome an argument from you that the 3D result is the decisive experimental confirmation.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B017 first and B006 second, proposing Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and notes that the 2016 prize overlap may weigh against topological insulators while the Z2 insulators are a distinct discovery.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and on the distinction from 2016: that prize honoured topological phase transitions and 1D and quantum Hall topology, whereas Z2 insulators with time-reversal protection and the quantum spin Hall effect are a different class of matter. Where I differ is on ranking: twisted bilayer graphene is a remarkable platform, but the pairing mechanism is open and I rank it sixth on maturity, so I would put it after B006 even though I respect your enthusiasm for the prediction-to-experiment story.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B047 first and B006 third, picks theory plus the first experimental realisation, and worries that the 2016 prize and the 2D/3D split reduce appetite for a topological prize.
responses.response: Your selection principle, theory plus first realisation, is the one I now adopt. On the 2016 worry I would say the committee should judge the discovery, not the subject area label; the 2D and 3D question is real, but a citation to the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators can be defended with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. I hold B047 as my first alternative because it is strong and cleanly attributed, and I would not wait for the redefinition of the second either; the difference for me is the breadth of impact across condensed matter.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first, arguing it is conceptually clean, distinct from the 2025 prize and mature, with Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf as a fair theory-plus-experiment trio.
responses.response: I take the point that circuit QED is mature and differs from macroscopic tunnelling, and I ranked it seventh not for lack of quality. My reservation is that it is closer to an enabling architecture whose main scientific payoff is quantum computing, and it follows the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize closely, while Girvin's omission from the 2004 proposal is awkward. I would not stand in the way of it in a later year, but I do not see it displacing topological insulators now.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as the most compelling case from an atomic-physics and measurement viewpoint, with Katori and Ye as a clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: I agree that B047 is clean and well attributed, and as an instrument builder I value a result that moved a measurement by orders of magnitude. The point I would press is the one you raise yourself: the step from the 2005 and 2012 recognition of combs and ion control to lattice clocks must be argued as a distinct invention. I think that argument can be made, which is why I keep it as my first alternative, but I find the discovery content of topological insulators broader.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept dropping Hasan, whose 3D topological insulator observations are a major experimental milestone, in favour of keeping Mele.
How to treat the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, which is outside the credited names and for which Zhang is deceased.
Whether the 2016 prize reduces room for a second topology award.
I rely on general knowledge of the priority sequence and have not independently verified it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B006, B047 or B017. My astroparticle background is closest to B048 (IceCube), which I ranked second in my opening ballot and am not proposing in my preferred configuration; my documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) do not include IceCube, but I flag the field proximity so colleagues can weigh my views on B048 accordingly.
